Recommended diagnostic contract: perturb only nonpadding history items, retain the most recent L items, then left-pad with zero. Score candidates through predict_score using log2feats at the last nonzero position; for nonempty, correctly left-padded sequences this is index L−1, not count_nonzero−1. Skip empty histories explicitly. Original SASRec uses right-aligned histories and final-timestep scoring. For full-catalog unseen recommendations, exclude zero and every item in the original observed training history, including items removed by perturbation or truncation; keep this candidate pool fixed across comparisons. Resolve equal scores deterministically by ascending item ID, using stable descending sorting over initially ID-sorted candidates. This is a diagnostic convention; preserve the host evaluator’s ranking rules. Sources: [SASRec preprocessing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kang205/SASRec/master/util.py), [scoring](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py), [stable sorting](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.sort.html).

Make inference observational: save every module’s training flag, call model.eval(), run under torch.inference_mode(), and restore individual flags in finally, preserving mixed submodule modes. Inference mode alone does not disable dropout. Use separate, explicitly seeded Python Random, NumPy Generator, and torch.Generator instances for user selection, perturbations, and sampling; derive seeds from stable identifiers, avoiding Python hash(). Preserve global Python/NumPy RNG states and use torch.random.fork_rng for CPU and the active CUDA device. Avoid iterating the live training loader: iterator creation can consume RNG, while sampling, worker prefetch, and persistent workers advance additional state. Prefer immutable history snapshots or a separate diagnostic loader with independent generators and workers; restoring generator states alone cannot rewind a consumed live iterator. Sources: [inference mode](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/generated/torch.autograd.grad_mode.inference_mode.html), [RNG isolation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/random.html), [DataLoader behavior](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/2.14/data.html).
